titulo: The camera as a verb: each movement tells something
lead: Camera movement weighs heavily on the result of a generated video, and a common mistake is stacking movements in the same shot. In this lesson each movement gets a function: move closer, pull back, follow, reveal, orbit, or shake. One per shot, chosen for its effect on the audience.
objetivo: choose one movement per shot by intent and write, for each shot, the effect it causes in whoever is watching.

aprende.t: Match six intentions to the movements that deliver them
Tell camera movement apart from lens movement
Use one movement and one style per shot
Vary the movement between neighboring shots

hero_alt: A film camera on a dolly track in a dark studio, with a crane arm in the background.

secoes.sub: Start with what the audience should feel. Click to see the movement and the prompt term.

nos.detalhe: A slow push in, the camera moving toward the subject: tension, intimacy, importance. In English, dolly in or push-in. Barely noticeable, the pressure builds.
Pulling back: the camera moves away and the place swallows the character. Isolation, scale, end of scene. In English, dolly out or pull-out.
Tracking: the camera moves along with the subject, from the side or behind. Flow, following without cutting. In English, tracking shot or truck left/right.
A pan (turns horizontally), a tilt (turns vertically) and a crane (rises or lowers through space) reveal what was outside the frame. In English, pan, tilt, crane shot, pedestal.
Orbit: the camera circles the subject and separates foreground, midground and background. Volume and the feel of an expensive film. In English, orbit or arc shot.
Handheld camera: unsteady, raw, documentary. Urgency and physical presence. In English, handheld shot.

secoes.legenda: A still camera (static shot) is also a choice: watching without interfering. It counts as "one movement" in the shot.

secoes.sub: The example continues in the bakery.

texto: Orbit plus push in plus pan plus zoom: the camera fights itself and the shot comes out unstable. One movement gives the generator a single direction to carry out.
If the scene calls for two movements, it calls for two shots.

exemplo.texto: Weak: an orbit with a zoom and a dolly on the oven. Directed: a slow push in on the oven while the door opens.

texto: In a dolly the camera moves: foreground and background shift at different rates and the space feels real. In a zoom only the lens changes: the image gets closer without the camera leaving its spot, flatter and more observational.
The dolly zoom does both at the same time, in opposite directions: the background seems to stretch. It's disorienting; use it once, at the right moment.
Style is the texture of the movement. Steadicam is smooth and controlled; handheld is raw and urgent; slow motion stretches time and gives weight.
Two styles in the same shot dilute both intentions. Pick the dominant feeling and stick with it.

Two neighboring shots with the same movement kill the rhythm. Match the movement to the job of the moment: opening calls for a side tracking shot or a still camera; tension calls for a slow move in; a reveal calls for an orbit or a tilt.
To close, use a final move in, or a pull back that gives the place back. End on a strong image.

revealing horizontally → pan → pan left, pan right

exercicios.titulo: Movements · one per shot, with the effect
exercicios.texto: For each shot in your scene, choose a movement (or a still camera) and write the effect on the audience. At least 4 different movements, with no repeats in neighboring shots. Check it and download movimentos.txt into the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page answers OK: [n] shots, one movement each, with the effect written for your text, and movimentos.txt is in the project folder.

exercicios.titulo: Neighbors · no movement repeated in a row
exercicios.texto: Read the list from top to bottom and mark where two neighboring shots use the same movement. Swap one of them for the movement that delivers the same intention in a different way.
exercicios.pronto: in movimentos.txt, no pair of neighboring shots repeats the same movement, and the page keeps answering OK: ….

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation shows up after each answer.

perguntas.p: What is the difference between a dolly in and a zoom in?
opcoes: None: both bring the subject closer in the same way.
The zoom moves the camera; the dolly changes the lens.
The dolly only works on a wide shot.
The dolly moves the camera; the zoom changes the lens.
perguntas.explica: In a dolly, the camera moves through space, and foreground and background shift at different rates, which creates depth. In a zoom, the camera stays still and only the focal length changes; the image looks flatter.

perguntas.p: A prompt asks for "orbit, dolly in and zoom" in the same shot. What is likely to come out?
opcoes: A premium shot, with more energy.
The generator picks the best of the three.
A longer shot, in three parts.
perguntas.explica: Stacked movements give conflicting directions, and the result comes out unstable. One movement per shot; if the scene calls for three movements, it calls for three shots.

perguntas.p: You want the tension to build while the oven door opens. Which movement?
perguntas.explica: The slow push-in builds pressure almost without the audience noticing. The whip pan is a fast transition; the pull-back isolates and closes; the handheld camera brings urgency, not anticipation.

perguntas.p: Two neighboring shots have the same movement. What do you do?
opcoes: Vary one of them, based on the scene's rhythm.
Merge the two into a single, bigger shot.
perguntas.explica: Repeating the same movement back to back kills the rhythm. Swap one of the two for a movement that delivers the same intention in a different way, or for a still camera.

itens.texto: Push in, pull back, follow, reveal, orbit, shake: each one makes the audience feel something different.
One movement and one style. Two movements call for two shots.
A dolly moves and gives depth; a zoom only brings the image closer.
